crossrefs.text: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.
with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
Therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience.
But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.
Whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked.
Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
By Myself I have sworn; truth has gone out from My mouth, a word that will not be revoked: Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance.
In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be justified and will exult.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps:
Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.
Therefore, since Christ suffered in His body, arm yourselves with the same resolve, because anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.
equip you with every good thing to do His will. And may He accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
He has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began.
For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,
So then, it does not depend on manʼs desire or effort, but on Godʼs mercy.
“Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?” Jesus answered,
“Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
Then Jesus told His disciples, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.
as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
Like ravenous dogs, they are never satisfied. They are shepherds with no discernment; they all turn to their own way, each one seeking his own gain:
I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.
But we ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who care for you in the Lord and who admonish you.
Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved fellow worker,
to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets at your house:
